stories.Headline: Palladyne AI (NASDAQ:PDYN) CFO Trevor Thatcher Sells 4,636 Shares of Stock
stories.Summary:
Palladyne AI's Chief Financial Officer Trevor Thatcher sold 4,636 shares of company stock on August 21st at an average price of $6.16 per share, generating $28,557.76 in total proceeds. Following this transaction, Thatcher retained 319,602 shares valued at approximately $1.97 million, representing a 1.43% reduction in his ownership stake. The sale was filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission as required.

The company has a market capitalization of $302.45 million with stock trading near $6.13. Palladyne AI recently reported quarterly earnings that missed analyst expectations, showing a loss of $0.27 per share against forecasts of $0.23, while revenue of $5.78 million fell slightly short of the projected $5.80 million. Analyst ratings on the stock remain mixed, with three buy ratings, two holds, and one sell recommendation, and a consensus price target of $11.00.

stories.Headline: UAE Business: Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank names new AI head
stories.Summary:
Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank has appointed Pedro Uria-Recio as its new Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer. The appointment strengthens the bank's leadership as it pursues its Vision 2035 strategy, which aims to make ADIB the world's most innovative Islamic bank. Uria-Recio will lead the bank's AI initiatives, focusing on enhancing customer experiences, improving risk management, and increasing operational efficiency while building the necessary capabilities and governance structures to scale AI responsibly across the organization.

Uria-Recio brings over 20 years of experience in technology, data, and artificial intelligence. He previously served as Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer at CIMB Bank in Malaysia, where he directed AI strategy and oversaw deployment of advanced analytics solutions across Southeast Asia. He has also held senior positions at True Corporation, Axiata Group, and McKinsey and Company. The bank's CEO emphasized that AI is a key transformation enabler for their strategy and that Uria-Recio's expertise will be essential for responsible, large-scale AI adoption throughout the organization.

stories.Headline: Oman's first AI SEZ to attract RO 106 million, construction to start in 2027
stories.Summary:
Oman is developing its first artificial intelligence special economic zone, which is expected to attract approximately 106 million Omani rials, equivalent to about 275 million dollars. The project will be developed over three phases across roughly 104,000 square meters near Muscat International Airport. Construction on the first phase is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027. The zone will be operated by Afouq Investment and Development United.

The AI zone will include business incubators, accelerators, robotics labs, research centers, data centers, and cloud computing facilities. Planners are negotiating with major technology companies like Microsoft and IBM to participate, and are also working with international universities to establish an AI-focused university in the zone. The initiative aims to support Oman's Vision 2040 goals by developing local technology startups into major companies and increasing the digital economy's contribution to GDP to approximately ten percent by 2040.
Orgs: public authority for special economic zones

stories.Headline: "Hardly any" AI regulations? Becerra should know better – Daily News
stories.Summary:
California gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra recently claimed that the state has "hardly any" artificial intelligence regulations. However, this statement contradicts the reality of California's regulatory landscape. According to Stanford's AI Index, California has enacted more AI-specific laws than any other state, including dozens of statutes passed in the last two years alone. Additionally, federal agencies and state attorneys general have confirmed that existing laws against discrimination, fraud, and unfair practices already apply to artificial intelligence systems.

Beyond specific AI legislation, California continues to add more regulations to the industry. Nearly twenty AI bills were signed into law in 2024, with additional legislation enacted in 2025 covering transparency and chatbot safeguards. Two dozen more AI bills are awaiting floor votes before an August 31 deadline. Meanwhile, some California localities have imposed moratoriums or bans on data centers, which are essential infrastructure for AI operations. The authors argue that California's regulatory approach may discourage technology development and innovation in the state.

stories.Headline: China's Inner Mongolia ramps up green computing, AI service exports
stories.Summary:
Inner Mongolia's autonomous region announced major expansion plans for its green computing and artificial intelligence industries at a conference in Hohhot on Saturday. Twelve projects valued at approximately 186.46 billion yuan, or 27.49 billion U.S. dollars, were signed at the event. The initiatives involve major companies including ByteDance's Volcano Engine, Cambricon Technologies, and China Telecom, and focus on developing intelligent computing centers, token factories, and manufacturing facilities for computing and electrical equipment.

Officials also launched construction on a new digital services platform designed to connect international developers with China's artificial intelligence models and green computing resources. The platform will assist Chinese artificial intelligence companies in expanding into overseas markets and provide services such as compliance assessment, computing-power distribution, and cross-border settlement. Inner Mongolia has become a major computing hub, with two regional areas operating computing capacity exceeding 300,000 petaflops combined, driven by the region's abundant wind and solar resources for powering data centers.

stories.Headline: Billionaires Stanley Druckenmiller and Dan Loeb Both Sold Broadcom and Piled Into This Virtual Monopoly Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Instead
stories.Summary:
Two prominent Wall Street investors, Stanley Druckenmiller and Dan Loeb, have made identical portfolio moves that signal shifting sentiment in the artificial intelligence sector. Both investors completely sold their Broadcom positions while simultaneously building stakes in Alphabet. Druckenmiller, a macro specialist who previously worked under George Soros, and Loeb, founder of the hedge fund Third Point, are known for their ability to rotate capital into emerging growth opportunities before consensus catches up. Their coordinated exit from Broadcom suggests they believe better risk-reward opportunities exist elsewhere in the AI ecosystem, despite Broadcom's central role in supplying components for AI data center infrastructure.

The investors' pivot toward Alphabet reflects confidence in the company's vertical integration strategy for artificial intelligence. Alphabet designs its own silicon called Tensor Processing Units, operates extensive data center and fiber networks, and develops AI models through its DeepMind lab under the Gemini family. The company leverages these capabilities across Google Search, YouTube, Android, and Workspace, creating what analysts describe as near-monopoly positioning in online search. Alphabet reported strong recent results with total revenue of 119.8 billion dollars, a 24 percent year-over-year increase, while Google Cloud revenue surged 82 percent to 24.8 billion dollars with a 514 billion dollar backlog.

stories.Headline: Billionaire David Tepper Sold His Fund's Sandisk Stake in Favor of This Trillion-Dollar Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock
stories.Summary:
David Tepper, who runs hedge fund Appaloosa Management, sold his entire Sandisk position in the second quarter and used the proceeds to buy Broadcom stock. Tepper had initiated the Sandisk investment in the first quarter and exited completely in the second quarter, securing substantial gains after the stock's dramatic rise. The move reflects disciplined profit-taking since memory markets are cyclical and Sandisk's recent valuation may have already priced in near-term artificial intelligence demand.

Broadcom designs custom artificial intelligence chips for major tech companies like Google, Meta, Apple, OpenAI, and Anthropic, plus supplies networking equipment connecting AI accelerators. Although Broadcom trades at a high valuation, the company expects to generate over one hundred billion dollars in AI revenue by fiscal 2027 and maintains strong competitive advantages through multi-year customer contracts. Tepper's decision to shift from a high-flying memory stock to a broader AI infrastructure company suggests investors should study his underlying investment thesis rather than simply copying his trades.

stories.Headline: AI for Good: How the UN uses AI to advance human rights
stories.Summary:
# Summary

The United Nations is utilizing artificial intelligence across multiple agencies to advance human rights and address global challenges. UNICEF's Accessible Digital Textbooks for All program now operates in 17 countries, serving nearly two million children with disabilities, and aims to expand to 50 countries by 2030. Meanwhile, the UN Environment Programme launched the Methane Alert and Response System in 2024, which uses AI to analyze satellite data and has issued 7,500 alerts since then, preventing methane emissions equivalent to 24 million gas-powered cars. The World Health Organization supports developing countries in using AI to analyze chest X-rays for tuberculosis detection, enabling faster diagnosis in areas with limited medical specialists.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called artificial intelligence both humanity's greatest opportunity and greatest risk in the 21st century, emphasizing the need for worldwide controls on AI development. The organization established a Global Dialogue on AI and an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI in 2025 to ensure the technology promotes development while protecting peace, democracy, and human rights. UNESCO adopted the first global AI ethics standard in 2021, while the UN launched a global network to expand AI capacity in developing countries.

stories.Headline: Billionaire Stephen Mandel Just Loaded Up on This Incredible Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Up Nearly 200% in 2026
stories.Summary:
Billionaire investor Stephen Mandel, who manages Lone Pine Capital hedge fund, recently added Nebius, an artificial intelligence cloud computing company, as his largest portfolio holding in the second quarter of 2026. Nebius stock has surged nearly 200 percent this year and operates in the neocloud space, providing AI-focused computing power to major technology companies. The company serves as a preferred partner of Nvidia and gains early access to cutting-edge technology.

Nebius has demonstrated exceptional growth, with revenue increasing 454 percent year over year in the second quarter. Analysts predict the company will continue expanding rapidly, forecasting 523 percent growth for the second half of 2026 and 258 percent growth in 2027. The strong demand for AI computing capacity positions Nebius favorably in the industry, as the company has signed agreements with major AI companies to rent them computing power.

stories.Headline: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Just Sold Some Sandisk Stock and Bought These 3 Unstoppable Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks
stories.Summary:
Billionaire hedge fund manager Stanley Druckenmiller sold some of his Sandisk stock during the second quarter and redirected those funds into three artificial intelligence-focused companies: Taiwan Semiconductor, Alphabet, and Amazon. Druckenmiller made this strategic shift after Sandisk had already experienced significant gains early in the year, making it prudent to take profits. His portfolio moves became public through required regulatory filings that large investment funds must submit quarterly.

The three stocks Druckenmiller purchased are positioned to benefit substantially from the artificial intelligence infrastructure expansion. Taiwan Semiconductor, the world's largest logic chip manufacturer, will see increased demand as AI computing requires more advanced chips. Meanwhile, Alphabet and Amazon are benefiting through their cloud computing divisions, with both companies planning to spend at least 200 billion dollars this year on capital expenditures to build new data centers. Since the full financial impact of these massive investments has not yet materialized in their earnings, these stocks have significant room for future growth.
